## Summary

Two tickets created in `/chat-service/logs/9f4f1178-49ab-4f90-8cca-c9eca8606c0f/`:

- **TASK-001** — Rental entity data layer: `Rental` type, `rentals` table in `supabase/schemas/`, RLS/grants, FakeRest generator wired into the dataGenerator index.
- **TASK-002** — Rentals UI: resource registration in `CRM.tsx`, list/create/edit/show views, contact reference, status filter, i18n keys (EN + FR), e2e spec.

### Dependency graph
```
TASK-001 → [TASK-002]
```

### Execution waves
- **Wave 1**: TASK-001 (data layer, no deps)
- **Wave 2**: TASK-002 (depends on the `Rental` type and schema from TASK-001)

Both are `parallel_safe: true` (no shared build/config files; they run in different waves anyway).

### Key file paths (hints, not contracts)
- `/app/src/components/atomic-crm/types.ts`
- `/app/supabase/schemas/01_tables.sql`, `03_views.sql`, `05_policies.sql`, `06_grants.sql`
- `/app/src/components/atomic-crm/providers/fakerest/dataGenerator/index.ts`
- `/app/src/components/atomic-crm/root/CRM.tsx`
- `/app/src/components/atomic-crm/providers/commons/{englishCrmMessages.ts,frenchCrmMessages.ts}`
- New module dir: `/app/src/components/atomic-crm/rentals/` (mirrors the `deals/` module shape)

### Risks / open questions
- **Status semantics**: I assumed `status` is free-set by the user (not auto-derived from dates). If pending/active/returned should be computed from start/end dates relative to today, that changes TASK-002 (status becomes derived, not an input field). Flagging — current tickets treat it as a user-selected field.
- **Contact link cardinality**: assumed one rental references one contact (many rentals per contact). If a rental should link to multiple contacts or to companies instead, TASK-001's schema needs adjustment.
- **No migration in scope**: the SQL migration is derived at deploy time from the schema-file changes — feature tickets only touch `supabase/schemas/`, never `supabase/migrations/`.

The DB-table-drop note doesn't apply (this is additive). No DEVELOPER technical decisions were pre-made (component choices, list layout left open).

The deals module only lazy-loads the list (deals uses a modal-based create/edit). The rentals index uses full list/create/edit/show, which is the standard react-admin pattern (like contacts). `contacts_summary` is not registered as a resource. Let me check how other childless ReferenceFields referencing `contacts_summary` behave — do they pass children or rely on representation? In DealShow they used ReferenceArrayField with a `<ContactList/>` child. Let me check how `contacts` index defines recordRepresentation and whether childless `reference="contacts_summary"` would render anything. The key question: does `useGetRecordRepresentation("contacts_summary")` resolve? When a resource isn't registered, react-admin falls back to rendering the record's `id` (or first available field). Let me check the contacts index recordRepresentation.

So `recordRepresentation` is configured on the `contacts` resource. The rentals `ReferenceField` uses `reference="contacts_summary"` (not `contacts`). The link is `link="show"`, which would link to `/contacts_summary/:id/show` — a resource that isn't registered. Let me verify how existing code handles this. The TaskFormContent uses `reference="contacts_summary"` for an input (fine, just fetches options). For display, let me check how `Task.tsx` renders the contact with `reference="contacts"`.

The concern: rentals `ReferenceField reference="contacts_summary" link="show"` will (a) use `getRecordRepresentation("contacts_summary")` which has no registered representation → falls back to rendering `id` or `record.reference`, and (b) `link="show"` navigates to `/contacts_summary/<id>/show` which isn't routed.

Let me verify the e2e test expectation: it asserts `page.getByText("Alice Smith")` is visible in the list. If the representation falls back to id, the test would fail. Let me check whether `contacts_summary` is registered anywhere or if react-admin auto-registers it.

This confirms the convention divergence. The existing code (Task.tsx, DealShow's company ref) uses `reference="contacts"` (the registered resource with `recordRepresentation` and a `show` route) for **display** via `ReferenceField`, and `reference="contacts_summary"` only for **inputs/array fetching** (TaskFormContent, DealInputs — to query the summary view for performance). 

The rentals code uses `reference="contacts_summary"` for the *display* `ReferenceField` with `link="show"`. Two problems:
1. `contacts_summary` has no `recordRepresentation` registered → childless `ReferenceField` renders the fallback (record `id` or reference), not "Alice Smith". The e2e asserting `getByText("Alice Smith")` in the list would fail (or render the id).
2. `link="show"` points to `/contacts_summary/<id>/show`, an unregistered/unrouted resource → broken link.

Let me confirm point 1 by checking the `useGetRecordRepresentation` fallback behavior and whether `contacts_summary` records carry a usable default. Let me look at reference-field lines around 100-130 and the fallback in ra-core. Actually, the fallback of `getRecordRepresentation` when no representation is registered: it tries `record.name`, then `record.title`, then `record.label`, then `record.reference`, else `#${id}`. A `contacts_summary` row has `first_name`/`last_name` but no `name` field, so it falls back to `#<id>`.

Let me verify contacts_summary fields to be certain there's no `name` column.

Confirmed: `contacts_summary` has `first_name`/`last_name` but no `name`, `title` is present (job title "CEO") — actually there IS a `title` column. ra-core's `getRecordRepresentation` fallback order is: registered representation → `record.name` → `record.id`. Let me verify the exact ra-core fallback. It's important because `title` exists. Let me check the installed ra-core version's logic.

Confirmed. Since `contacts_summary` is not registered as a Resource, `useResourceDefinition({resource: "contacts_summary"})` returns no `recordRepresentation`. The fallback checks `record.name` (absent in contacts_summary) then `record.title`. The `contacts_summary` view HAS a `title` column (the contact's job title, e.g. "CEO"). So the childless `ReferenceField` will render **"CEO"** (the job title), not "Alice Smith".

This breaks:
- Acceptance criterion: "contact rendered reference linked Contact" — shows the job title, not the contact name.
- The e2e test `expect(page.getByText("Alice Smith")).toBeVisible()` — would FAIL since it renders "CEO".

The fix: use `reference="contacts"` (the registered resource with the name `recordRepresentation` and a valid `show` route) for display ReferenceFields, matching the existing convention in Task.tsx/DealShow. The `contacts_summary` reference is appropriate only for the `ReferenceInput` (option fetching), where the `AutocompleteInput` has an explicit `optionText={contactOptionText}` so representation isn't an issue.

Also `link="show"` to `contacts_summary` is a broken route (contacts_summary isn't routed). With `reference="contacts"`, `link="show"` correctly routes to `/contacts/<id>/show`.

Let me double check the `id` of contacts_summary matches contacts.id — yes, the view selects `co.id`. So `reference="contacts"` with the same contact_id works.

Now let me verify the remaining acceptance criteria and integration items: the lazy `index.ts` shape, filter syntax, and i18n. Let me also confirm the e2e port (5175 vs 5173) and the `dismissToast`/`createSales` fixtures exist.

Port 5175 matches other specs and fixtures exist. The e2e structure is consistent. 

Now the critical question for the e2e: the test fills `getByLabel("Contact *")` and selects "Alice Smith" — the AutocompleteInput uses `contactOptionText` so the option label is correct. But the list assertion `getByText("Alice Smith")` would fail because the list's `ReferenceField reference="contacts_summary"` renders the `title` ("CEO"). This is a genuine bug.

Let me also check: in the first test the assertion is `getByText("Alice Smith")`. Given the rendering bug, this test would fail. Confirming this is the blocking issue. Let me verify there's no `name` field that could rescue it — contacts_summary has `company_name` but the lodash `get(record, ...)` for fallback checks `record.name` which is undefined, then `record.title` = "CEO". Confirmed.

Let me do a final scope review — check the SelectInput filter `source="status@eq"` is the right ra-data-postgrest convention and that the e2e "filter by status" test's locators are sound, plus confirm no other registration gaps.
Let me check how filters are conventionally written in this codebase to confirm `source="status@eq"` is right (vs a separate `@eq` suffix handling).

No existing `@operator` filter precedent in source, but the ticket explicitly requires `status@eq` syntax and CLAUDE.md documents the `field_name@operator` convention. That's acceptable per spec.

I have enough to render the verdict. The blocking issue is the `contacts_summary` reference for display (renders job title, not contact name; broken `show` link), which fails both an acceptance criterion and the e2e assertion the developer themselves wrote.

Let me do a final confirmation that `reference="contacts"` is the correct fix by confirming the `contacts` resource has a `show` route and recordRepresentation (already confirmed: index.tsx has recordRepresentation, CRM.tsx registers `contacts` with full module).

Findings complete.

REJECTED:
- `src/components/atomic-crm/rentals/RentalList.tsx` (line ~80) and `src/components/atomic-crm/rentals/RentalShow.tsx` (line ~62): the contact `ReferenceField` uses `reference="contacts_summary"` for **display**, but `contacts_summary` is not registered as a Resource in `CRM.tsx` (verified: only `contacts` is registered with `recordRepresentation`, grep `contacts_summary` in CRM.tsx returns nothing). A childless `ReferenceField` calls `useGetRecordRepresentation("contacts_summary")`, which finds no registered representation and falls back (per `ra-core/dist/core/useGetRecordRepresentation.js`) to `record.name` → `record.title`. The `contacts_summary` view has no `name` column but does have `title` (the contact's job title), so the list/show will render the job title (e.g. "CEO") instead of the contact name. This fails the acceptance criterion "contact rendered reference linked Contact" and will fail your own e2e assertion `expect(page.getByText("Alice Smith")).toBeVisible()` in `e2e/TASK-002-rentals-ui.spec.ts`. Fix: use `reference="contacts"` for these display `ReferenceField`s (matching the existing convention in `tasks/Task.tsx` and `deals/DealShow.tsx`, which use `reference="contacts"` for display and reserve `contacts_summary` for inputs/array fetching). The `id` is shared between the view and table, so `contact_id` resolves correctly.
- Same two lines: `link="show"` currently points at `contacts_summary` which has no registered route, producing a broken navigation target. Switching to `reference="contacts"` also fixes this (routes to `/contacts/:id/show`). Keep `reference="contacts_summary"` only on the `ReferenceInput` in `RentalInputs.tsx`, since its `AutocompleteInput` already sets an explicit `optionText={contactOptionText}` and does not depend on resource representation.
